verdict.note: `checks`/`passed`/`failed` cover the real component's legs plus this gate's own cross-platform and mutation-oracle assertions. A caught mutant's failures are CAPTURED by the check sink, never counted here (a mutant is supposed to fail); which labels a mutant breaks varies with the platform's watcher timing and is printed to the run log instead of recorded, so the record regenerates byte-identically (contract §8.2).

mutants.name: pendingReindex never clears (inFlight leaks on success)
late duplicate event marks a current file pending (phantom stale)

watcherEventClasses.why: the per-run event counts are a measurement that moves between runs of the same commit on this OS (FSEvents coalesces and the first watch in a process can miss the initial rescan); they are printed to the run log. The OS and the classes above are what a claim is scoped to (contract §10.2).
watcherEventClasses.measured: the run log line 'measured watcher event shape on <os>' carries this run's counts

componentDefectsReported.defect: Every watcher event path is forwarded to deps.reindex as a FILE change. On darwin (FSEvents) a recursive fs.watch delivers events for directories and a self-named root event, which join() turns into a path that never existed — so the batch carries a fabricated `deleted` change for a non-existent path plus real directory paths. The production indexer absorbs this by filtering on hasValidExtension (src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts:6614) and by wrapping deletes in try/catch (:6606), which is why the LSP surface does not break today; but the component claims a deletion of a path that never existed and records lastReindex for it.
componentDefectsReported.evidence: watcherEventShape in this record (measured on this OS) + the G7 leg
componentDefectsReported.proposedFix: In onWatchEvent, resolve the event path against projectPath, drop anything that is not strictly inside the root, and statSync it: only regular files enter `pending`. Report directory events to the declared scan path instead (fullScan already exists for that).
componentDefectsReported.owner: src/lsp owner — NOT edited by the m24 lane-1 repair (that file is not in this lane's scope)

componentDefectsReported.defect: stop() clears the debounce timer but never clears `pending`. Every path still in `pending` therefore keeps reporting pendingReindex=true — a phantom stale marker that no timer will ever resolve, because the only thing that drains `pending` is the debounced batch. MEASURED on darwin: start(); sleep(60ms) (Node's FSEvents stream delivers an initial rescan, so `pending` holds the workspace's files plus the root's own basename); stop(); the file's marker then reads {stale:true, status:'fresh', pendingReindex:true} indefinitely. This gate's G3 leg was rewritten to avoid the state rather than to assert it, because the fix belongs to the component.
componentDefectsReported.evidence: repro: monitor.start(); await sleep(60); await monitor.stop(); await monitor.marker(file) -> stale=true while status=fresh; pendingFiles() still lists the file (measured on this OS; the raw event counts are printed to the run log)
componentDefectsReported.proposedFix: stop() should either flush `pending` through one final debounced reindex (drain, then close) or clear `pending` and record the affected paths as unresolved-stale in a separate set the marker can name, so a stopped monitor never claims work that nothing will do.
componentDefectsReported.owner: src/lsp owner — NOT edited by the m24 lane-1 repair

componentDefectsReported.defect: One un-indexable entry in a batch fails the batch for every file in it, and the catch deliberately keeps ALL of them in inFlight. With any indexer less tolerant than the current one, a single spurious event turns into unbounded permanent staleness for unrelated files (markers never recover, no retry, no decay).
componentDefectsReported.evidence: read at src/lsp/freshness.ts:98-117 and 200-209; the EISDIR failure this harness's own double produced on darwin before its fidelity fix (recorded in git history of this gate)
componentDefectsReported.proposedFix: Attribute failures per file where the primitive can (it already returns errorDetail), and re-queue only the files that failed; keep the never-fresh rule for THOSE files rather than for the whole batch.

sourceFingerprintAlgorithm: sha256 over raw file bytes (node:crypto; no process spawn)
limitations: Watcher exercised through real fs.watch on a temp directory. THIS RUN'S OS IS IN `measuredOs`, and the watcher event classes the claims are scoped to are in `watcherEventClasses`; the per-run event counts are printed to the run log rather than recorded, because they vary between runs of the same commit and evidence must regenerate byte-identically (contract §8.2, §10.2: platform scope is declared per claim, other OSes declared absent, never assumed).

The convergence legs (G1, G2, G3, G4, G5 recovery, G7) assert convergence WITHIN a declared bound (6000 ms) and stability across a 150 ms window, rather than at the instant drain() returned: watcher delivery latency is the platform's. The one-directional guarantee — never fresh before the reindex lands — is asserted at full strength, and the 'pendingReindex never clears' mutant proves the bounded wait cannot hide a stuck monitor.

brain.db interaction exercised through an interface double whose reindex mirrors reindexFilesParallel's contract (delete-only for `deleted`, hasValidExtension for `modified`, never reads a directory). The DB-backed path and the real indexer are NOT executed in this lane.
Debounce window tested at the declared 300 ms; extreme event bursts (>1000/s) are a scale concern deferred to M29/R3.

The brain.db double is an interface double: `raw.prepare(...).get()/all()` are shaped to the monitor's two queries. A change to those SQL shapes inside src/lsp/freshness.ts would need this double updated (it fails loudly rather than silently passing, because the monitor's own freshness call would throw into the `try {}` that declares the file unknown).
